decisionsForDave: D6 — Research scope, CT-DEC-13: A) Three-project Lot pilot after live services are measurable: Patch standards, Service training, Admission lanes B) Implement the same pilot before live services, against current outcomes; more rework risk C) Defer all research; leave CT-DEC-13 Proposed Recommended: A. OPEN.

D7 — Ownership and economy scope: A) Keep rentals for the first live-show slice; add ownership afterward B) Ownership and ledger first. More persistent business depth, larger save and accounting work C) Rentals only for this release; no ownership milestone Recommended: A. OPEN.

D8 — Existing sprite library: A) Inventory provenance now; retain during prototype; archive unused art once replacements are accepted B) Keep every asset as a permanent library. Lowest transition risk, ongoing size/style debt C) Commission or regenerate all art immediately. Highest cost before renderer dimensions are proven Recommended: A. OPEN.

D9 — CT-DEC-10 Lot economy and progression: A) Keep current numbers experimental; conduct paired strategy tests and a human career before accepting B) Accept the present Lot goals and deal/relationship rules now; fun still needs testing C) Prioritize retuning first: make PA/lights situationally worthwhile and compare door/guarantee strategies before expansion Recommended: A. OPEN.

D10 — CT-DEC-11 later rooms: A) Keep implemented room behavior experimental while venue art and tier-specific tests develop B) Accept current behavior: grid Club, returnable Lot, house rigs, seated multi-night shell, two-stage grounds C) Reopen room mechanics before art: specify fixed-room versus grid behavior and future stage scheduling first Recommended: A. OPEN.

D11 — When may the game be promoted publicly?: A) Wait for the 3D Lot and live-operations pilot plus existing release gates B) Promote the current playable once existing provenance, design and human acceptance gates pass; label it early access C) Keep it unlisted without a launch milestone for now Recommended: A. OPEN.
